title: TT-Lang · Vector addition
content:
{"zh": "# TT-Lang · 向量加法

用 TT-Lang 实现 FP32 向量加法 **out = a + b**，N 介于 1 与 16,777,217 之间。

提交一个 Python 文件，定义：

```python
import ttl

@ttl.operation(grid=(1, 1))
def vector_add(a, b, out):
    ...
```

## 评测方式

评测器导入你的文件，只调用名为 **`vector_add`** 的 operation（签名见上），不会调用其他内容。输入已经是
device 0 上的 **FP32、tile 布局、DRAM** 张量，输出张量 `out` 已预分配并清零。不要自己打开/关闭设备，不要读
stdin，也不要打印答案。只有 TT-Lang operation 在硬件上运行；文件里的主机代码只在导入时执行一次。

填充规则：评测器把 `a`、`b` 用零补到 `P = 1024 × ceil(N / 1024)` 个元素，并以 `(P / 32, 32)` 的 tile 形状上传；`out` 形状相同。只检查 `out` 按行优先展开后的前 N 个值。

正确性：每个逻辑输出元素需满足 `|got - want| <= 1e-06 + 0.00390625 × scale`，其中 scale 为 每个元素的 |a| + |b|。
FPU 会把 FP32 操作数舍入到约 11 位有效数字，所以容差比 FP32 的 epsilon 宽；`ttl.exp` 等 SFPU 函数保持 FP32 精度。

## 测试用例

| # | N | padded tiles |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 31 | 1 |
| 3 | 33 | 1 |
| 4 | 1,023 | 1 |
| 5 | 1,024 | 1 |
| 6 | 1,025 | 2 |
| 7 | 65,537 | 65 |
| 8 | 1,048,577 | 1025 |
| 9 | 16,777,216 | 16384 |
| 10 | 16,777,217 | 16385 |

输入由固定随机种子生成，所有提交看到相同数据。

## 限制与配额

- 串行评测，**每个用例 180 秒墙钟**（含 TT-Lang 编译），8 GB 主机内存。
- **本题总共最多接受 200 次提交**（所有账号合计，含 pretest）。题目页面会显示已用次数，请先在本地测试。
- 运行环境：tt-lang `1.1.10.dev20260921`（自带 ttnn，Blackhole p300c），支持 `ttl.grid_size(dims=1)` 与
  `ttl.node(dims=1)`。起始代码见附件 `starter.py`。

## 性能剖析

每个通过的用例都会在记录页返回性能摘要。计分用的是**设备时间**：在单独的插桩 pass 中（5 次热身、10 次采样），
从所有核心上第一个 kernel 开始到最后一个 kernel 结束的时间，取采样中位数；不含主机调度、JIT 编译和数据传输。
**排行榜**按 10 个用例设备时间的几何平均排名，每个账号只列最快的一次通过提交，并显示相对单核参考解
（22.1 µs）的加速比。报告里请使用设备时间。

记录页还会显示 kernel 使用的核数、**有效带宽**（题目必须读写的字节数除以设备时间；Blackhole DRAM 峰值约 512 GB/s）、
每个核心各 RISC 的 kernel cycles，以及仅供诊断的主机端调用计时。
", "en": "# TT-Lang · Vector addition

Implement **out = a + b** for FP32 vectors of length N (1 ≤ N ≤ 16,777,217) as a TT-Lang operation.

Submit one Python file that defines:

```python
import ttl

@ttl.operation(grid=(1, 1))
def vector_add(a, b, out):
    ...
```

## How the judge runs your code

The judge imports your file and calls the operation named **`vector_add`** exactly as shown in the signature; it
never calls anything else. Inputs are already **FP32, tile-layout tensors in device DRAM** on device 0 and the
output tensor `out` is preallocated with zeros. Do not open or close the device, do not read stdin and do not
print the answer. Only the TT-Lang operation runs on hardware; host-side code in your file runs once at import.

Padding: the judge pads `a` and `b` with zeros to `P = 1024 * ceil(N / 1024)` values and uploads them as `(P / 32, 32)` tiles; `out` has the same shape. Only the first N values of `out` (row-major) are checked.

Correctness: every logical output element must satisfy `|got - want| <= 1e-06 + 0.00390625 x scale`, where
scale is |a| + |b| per element. The FPU rounds FP32 operands to about 11 significant bits, so the tolerance is deliberately
wider than FP32 epsilon; `ttl.exp` and other SFPU functions keep FP32 precision.

## Test cases

| # | N | padded tiles |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 31 | 1 |
| 3 | 33 | 1 |
| 4 | 1,023 | 1 |
| 5 | 1,024 | 1 |
| 6 | 1,025 | 2 |
| 7 | 65,537 | 65 |
| 8 | 1,048,577 | 1025 |
| 9 | 16,777,216 | 16384 |
| 10 | 16,777,217 | 16385 |

Inputs are generated from a fixed seed, so every submission sees the same data.

## Limits and quota

- One case at a time, **180 s wall time per case** including TT-Lang compilation, and 8 GB host memory.
- **This problem accepts at most 200 submissions in total**, counted over all accounts (pretests included).
  The problem page shows how many are used. Test locally first; you cannot buy back a wasted submission.
- Runtime: tt-lang `1.1.10.dev20260921` (bundled ttnn, Blackhole p300c). `ttl.grid_size(dims=1)` and
  `ttl.node(dims=1)` are supported in this version. The starter file is attached as `starter.py`.

## Profile summary

Every accepted case returns a profile summary on the record page. The number that counts is the
**device time**: in a separate instrumented pass (5 warmups, 10 samples), the time from the first kernel
start to the last kernel end over all cores, median over the samples. It excludes host dispatch, JIT
compilation and data transfers. The submission's score for the **leaderboard** is the geometric mean of the
device times of the 10 testcases; the leaderboard lists each account's fastest accepted submission
and its speedup over the single-core reference (22.1 µs). Report device times in your report.

The record page also shows the cores your kernel used, its **effective bandwidth** (the bytes the problem must
read and write divided by device time; Blackhole DRAM peaks at about 512 GB/s), per-RISC kernel cycles per core
and, for diagnosis only, host-side timing of the call.
"}
